solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Respecting a law about health resorts?

indicators.note: about can mean around or in a jumble, so these letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A legal question concerning spa towns, as if a lawyer were asking which statute governs them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the anagram signal: RESPECTINGALAW rearranges to the fourteen letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spa towns where visitors once came to take the waters are known by this older phrase.

clue.text: Temporarily stop using song in bad taste?

parts.note: a lay is an old word for a song or ballad
a remark that is a bit off is unacceptable or in poor taste

explanation.surface: A tasteless song prompts someone to stop singing it for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to cease using or doing something for a period, as in easing up on a habit.

clue.text: Language of a shortened New Testament risks being misconstrued

indicators.note: something misconstrued is read wrongly, so these letters are taken out of order

parts.note: NT is the standard shortening of New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone warns that translating a Biblical text into another tongue risks misinterpretation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being misconstrued' tells you to rearrange A, NT and RISKS together.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient classical tongue of India, used in Hindu scriptures, is one example of a language.

clue.text: Proper men chat about restoration of harmony

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so these letters are shuffled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Respectable gentlemen hold a conversation on the subject of making peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of' but is the anagram signal for PROPERMENCHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for re-establishing friendly relations, especially between nations, after estrangement.

clue.text: Left work carrying suitable computer

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: Someone departs from the office, taking along the right machine for the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A portable personal machine for computing that rests on the user's knees.

clue.text: Bird in a river in S. American capital that's lost tail

indicators.note: in places one piece within another
losing its tail means the final letter of the city name goes

parts.note: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela

explanation.surface: A bird is spotted at a river running through a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's lost tail' drops the last S of CARACAS, leaving CARACA; 'in' puts A and R inside it, before the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon of Central and South America, related to hawks, is a type of bird.

clue.text: A crazy tax for keeping a bird

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one letter is placed within the rest

parts.note: mad means crazy
VAT is value added tax, a British sales tax

explanation.surface: A ridiculous levy is imposed on keeping a pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital A starts the answer; 'keeping' holds the lower-case a just before VAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The red avadavat, a small South Asian finch kept in cages, is a type of bird.

clue.text: Article penned by two parents in the country

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: pa and ma are a father and a mother
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece of writing composed jointly by a mother and father about a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts AN inside PA MA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American nation, home of the canal, is the country meant.

clue.text: Ten making shell anew? Alas, this lot couldn't achieve that!

definitions.text: Ten making shell anew? Alas, this lot couldn't achieve that!

indicators.note: anew means afresh or made again, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A group tries to rebuild a broken shell and fails, recalling Humpty Dumpty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anew' rearranges TENMAKINGSHELL. The nursery rhyme says the royal horses and soldiers couldn't put Humpty Dumpty, an egg, together again.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the monarch's soldiers failed to reassemble the broken egg Humpty Dumpty.

clue.text: Desire — it tends to dissipate if one's impartial

indicators.note: to dissipate is to scatter, so these letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone without bias finds that longing simply fades away.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unbiased, with no stake in the outcome, is the strict sense of this word.

clue.text: Small islands, source of surprise to you sailing west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
the source of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Tiny islands surprise a traveller heading west by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'sailing west' means read right to left; the pieces join to STOYE before turning.
explanation.definitionFit: Small river islands, especially in the Thames, are known by this old word, also spelt aits.

clue.text: Taliban moving into place for quasi-military game

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted around into a new order

explanation.surface: Insurgent fighters advance into a location, as in a war game.
explanation.definitionFit: A combat game in which players shoot each other with pellets of dye, mimicking soldiers.

clue.text: Deduce number in place beyond redemption?

parts.note: to infer is to deduce

explanation.surface: Someone works out a figure for a hopeless location.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante's hell, where the damned cannot be saved, is the place meant; the question mark flags the description.

clue.text: Challenge the veracity of beautiful person's claim?

definitions.meaning: to call a witness's honesty into question
a lovely person might boast of being a peach, and I am contracts to two letters

explanation.surface: A good-looking person's assertion is questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: A peach is a very attractive person, so such a person might say 'I'm a peach' without the article.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to discredit a witness's testimony is one sense of the verb.

clue.text: Hawk regrets a hit? That's odd for an aggressive creature

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the preceding letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A war hawk regrets a successful strike, which seems out of character.
explanation.definitionFit: The large predatory fish of the film Jaws is a fearsome and dangerous animal.

clue.text: Put in peril? No good being cross any more!

definitions.text: No good being cross any more!
definitions.meaning: split as a phrase, it urges finishing with fury

explanation.surface: Someone is told it's pointless staying angry once they've been put at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, END ANGER means stop being cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose to danger or risk is the plain verb sense.

clue.text: Flannel? Has it been in the bath too long?

definitions.meaning: flannel is British slang for flattery or smooth talk

definitions.text: Has it been in the bath too long?
definitions.meaning: a bar of washing material left in water goes squishy

explanation.surface: A washcloth question, then a worry about something left soaking in the tub.
explanation.walkthrough: Flannel looks like a washcloth here, but it means smooth persuasive talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery used to persuade someone is the idiomatic sense; literally it is a mushy bar.

clue.text: Boy with an 'orrible smell? Provide something fragrant

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the dropped H of horrible shows a Cockney accent that also drops the H of the next word

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: A lad with an awful odour is given something nice-smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orrible signals H-dropping, so HUM loses its H to give UM.
explanation.definitionFit: A gum resin from rockroses, used in perfumery, is a sweet-smelling substance.

clue.text: Stupid person as head

definitions.meaning: informal word for the skull or brain, as in use your loaf

explanation.surface: A simpleton is put in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a slang term for a silly person and a slang term for someone's head.

clue.text: Desist as sports official given reason for stopping play?

parts.note: a ref is a referee
rain often halts games such as cricket or tennis

explanation.surface: A referee holds back when the weather halts the game.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain or cease from an action is the verb sense, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A male essayist producing novel

parts.note: Elia was the pen name of Charles Lamb, the English essayist

explanation.surface: A man who writes essays produces a work of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fielding's last work of fiction bears this title, so it is an example of a book.

clue.text: Prisoners getting discovered inside making puzzles

indicators.note: inside means placed within, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: cons are convicts
found means discovered

explanation.surface: Inmates turn up hidden in the jail, baffling the guards.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle or perplex someone is the verb sense, a synonym.

clue.text: Crossword compilers — heartless folk full of wisdom!

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letters are removed

parts.note: setters are those who compose crosswords

explanation.surface: A jibe that puzzle makers are cruel, yet wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central TT out of SETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prophets and wise people who can foresee things are the meaning, a synonym.

clue.text: Seaside items the fellow will put into ship

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship
he'll contracts he will

explanation.surface: A man promises to load beach finds on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard coverings of molluscs, often collected on beaches, are typical items found by the sea.

clue.text: Possibly fine writer with a story enthralling son

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: A possibly good author with a tale that captivates their boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks fining as one way to punish; 'fine' looks like an adjective but is a verb. 'enthralling' puts S inside LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Imposing a monetary charge is one example of punishing someone.
